title: Inspection of supplies
text: FAMR 12.1 Inspection of supplies (2019.1). The Government shall inspect supplies at the contractor facility within 10 calendar days after delivery notice. Latent defects discovered after acceptance remain the contractor's responsibility for 90 days. The contracting officer may reject an entire lot if more than 2 percent of sampled units fail the specification in Attachment B.

title: Inspection of supplies
text: FAMR 12.1 Inspection of supplies (2023.1). The Government shall inspect supplies at the contractor facility within 5 calendar days after delivery notice. Latent defects discovered after acceptance remain the contractor's responsibility for 180 days. The contracting officer may reject an entire lot if more than 1 percent of sampled units fail the specification in Attachment B. Digital inspection records shall be retained for 3 years.

title: Inspection of supplies
text: FAMR 12.1 Inspection of supplies (2024.2). The Government shall inspect supplies at destination within 7 calendar days after delivery notice. Latent defects discovered after acceptance remain the contractor's responsibility for 365 days. Lot rejection uses a 1 percent sample-fail threshold. Digital inspection records shall be retained for 7 years and must include the inspector's identity credential.

title: Payment terms
text: FAMR 12.4 Payment terms (2018.4). The Government will pay proper invoices Net 30 days after receipt of a valid invoice and accepted supplies. No prompt-payment discount is offered. Interest on late payment follows the Prompt Payment Act rate then in effect.

title: Payment terms
text: FAMR 12.4 Payment terms (2022.1). The Government will pay proper invoices Net 45 days after receipt of a valid invoice and accepted supplies. A 1 percent prompt-payment discount applies if payment is made within 10 days. Interest on late payment follows the Prompt Payment Act rate then in effect.

title: Payment terms
text: FAMR 12.4 Payment terms (2023.4). The Government will pay proper invoices Net 30 days after receipt of a valid invoice and accepted supplies. A 2 percent prompt-payment discount applies if payment is made within 10 days. Small-business contractors may request Net 15. Interest on late payment follows the Prompt Payment Act rate then in effect.

title: Option to extend
text: FAMR 15.3 Option to extend (2020.2). The Government may extend the contract for one additional period of 6 months by written notice 30 days before the current period ends. Unit prices for the option period shall not increase by more than 3 percent.

title: Option to extend
text: FAMR 15.3 Option to extend (2024.1). The Government may extend the contract for one additional period of 12 months by written notice 60 days before the current period ends. Unit prices for the option period shall not increase by more than 2 percent. Exercise of the option requires a documented best-value determination.

title: Contractor ethics program
text: FAMR 52.13 Contractor ethics program (2019.3). Contractors with contracts above $5 million and a period of performance of 120 days or more shall maintain a written code of business ethics. Disclosure of credible evidence of fraud is required within 30 days of discovery.

title: Contractor ethics program
text: FAMR 52.13 Contractor ethics program (2023.2). Contractors with contracts above $6 million and a period of performance of 90 days or more shall maintain a written code of business ethics and an internal control system. Disclosure of credible evidence of fraud is required within 14 days of discovery. Mandatory training is annual.

title: Disputes forum
text: FAMR 33.2 Disputes forum (2017.1). Claims shall be submitted in writing to the contracting officer. Unresolved claims may be appealed to the Civilian Board of Contract Appeals within 90 days of the contracting officer's final decision. This clause has not been revised.

title: Small business subcontracting goal
text: FAMR 4.8 Small business subcontracting goal (2021.1). For contracts above $750,000 the contractor shall submit a subcontracting plan with a 23 percent small-business goal measured by obligated dollars.

title: Small business subcontracting goal
text: FAMR 4.8 Small business subcontracting goal (2025.1). For contracts above $750,000 the contractor shall submit a subcontracting plan with a 26 percent small-business goal measured by obligated dollars, including a 5 percent HUBZone subgoal.
